name: Servos page lists every servo in use and writes each one at its own index
step: Servos page lists every servo in use and writes each one at its own index
rationale:
From wingflight-firmware MSP API 22.16 a servo is a servo: servo N is sent on PWM
output N where the board has one and on channel N of a bus output (SBUS, F.Bus) when
one is set up. MSP_STATUS servo_count is the servos in use (the larger of the PWM
outputs and the servos a bus sends), index N is servo S(N+1) in every servo message,
and the servo record has no rate. The separate PWM and BUS pages became one Servos
page, and the PWM update rate became one setting in MSP_MIXER_CONFIG.

This replaces bin/pwm_servo_write (rotorflight-lua-ethos-suite PR #2555, Issue #2445),
which pinned the PWM page to the PWM outputs and to the raw write (cmd 124) because
cmd 212 used to take a packed index. That split no longer exists; what must not come
back is an offset between a tile and the index it writes.

No build and no package step reaches this -- it is a list and a save path through a
running page. The harness drives the real servos page with the real page runtime and
the real servo-config and mixer-config write builders, in five bench layouts: PWM
only, PWM with a 24-channel bus, a bus with no PWM outputs, a servo count past 24, and
a refused servo-timing read. It checks the tile count, that the PWM Rate tile is
there only with PWM outputs, that a save is one cmd 212 with the tile's own index and
the 15-byte record, that every tile's icon file exists, and that the rate is saved as
cmd 43 with the model type and bus channel counts echoed as read.
